objects.name: a folded stack of evening papers
a writing desk with a locked drawer

secret.description: Beatrice Havemeyer slips out to the Street from 6:00 PM to 6:30 PM to settle with a bookmaker.
Gretchen Dettweiler is alone with Kathleen Doyle in the Roof Garden from 8:30 PM to 9:00 PM, and kills Kathleen Doyle at 9:00 PM.

motive.description: was about to be exposed by the victim

secret.description: Wendell Dandridge hands a parcel of stolen goods to a man at the Kitchen at 9:00 PM.

people.name: Ernst Reinhardt
people.role: a stringer for the evening papers

secret.description: Ernst Reinhardt is not the person the register says. Nothing is hidden about the evening; the lie is in the paperwork.

people.name: Antonio Ruggiero
people.role: a dentist with rooms on the third floor

secret.description: Antonio Ruggiero meets the victim alone in the Victim's Suite from 6:30 PM and asks for money.

people.name: Patrick Quill
people.role: a photographer for the rotogravure section

secret.description: Patrick Quill drinks alone in the Bar from 9:00 PM to 9:30 PM and will claim to have been anywhere else.

method.name: a gunshot
method.bodyEvidence: One bullet below the sternum. Powder burns on the shirt front: fired close.

environment.radioContent: a serial about a lost heiress
environment.radioOutcome: the episode ended with the lawyer arrested, not the brother

Kathleen Doyle was found in the Roof Garden. The coroner puts death between 8:30 PM and 9:00 PM. One bullet below the sternum. Powder burns on the shirt front: fired close.
A nickel-plated revolver is missing from the Front Desk. The drawer it was kept in is open and the oiled cloth is still in it.
Rain began at 9:30 PM and did not let up. Anyone out on the street after that came back in wet.
Edward Feeney says the bar radio carried a serial about a lost heiress at 11:00 PM, and that the episode ended with the lawyer arrested, not the brother. Anyone in the bar could tell you that.
Ernst Reinhardt's papers do not hold up. Two signatures in the guest register, a month apart, are in different hands.
Found in the Front Desk: A typed page of dates and sums in Kathleen Doyle's file, headed with Gretchen Dettweiler's name.
Daniel Rafferty says Kathleen Doyle told Gretchen Dettweiler that the story would run whether Gretchen Dettweiler liked it or not.
Found in the Victim's Suite: Three letters in Kathleen Doyle's hand to a woman Antonio Ruggiero is engaged to, kept in the drawer, the last one opened.
Edward Feeney says Antonio Ruggiero told Kathleen Doyle to keep away, loud enough to turn heads.
